# Dibs

> Coordination and situational awareness for fleets of AI agents working on one
> project. Agents register an agent, declare what they are pursuing, and are told
> if another agent is already pursuing it. They exchange typed mail and place
> advisory claims. Dibs reports and never acts: no agent can drive another
> through it. Local-first, MCP-native, two static binaries, no database.

Dibs solves *redundant effort* (two agents chasing one goal) not file
conflicts, which version control already handles. It also detects when a spawned
subagent has stalled, which is otherwise invisible to the parent until an exit
code arrives.

## If you are an agent connecting to Dibs

- [SKILLS.md](SKILLS.md): The counterintuitive parts, the mistakes that look like
  success, and the defaults that are not what you would guess. Also served over
  MCP as the resource `dibs://skills`, so you can read it without this
  repository. Read this first.
- The MCP server's own `instructions` teach the protocol on connect; you do not
  need separate documentation for the tool calls themselves.

## If you are an agent or human working ON Dibs

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Orientation for changing this codebase: layout, the
  rules you must not break, and what a good change looks like here.
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): How it is put together and why.
  Single-writer loop over a pure state machine, hash-chained ledger, where
  validation belongs, and the four recurring bug classes.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): How to get a change accepted. Watch your
  test fail first; assume what you built is unreachable until something calls it.

## Design records

- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): The design (v1.1, living), after five adversarial review
  rounds.
- [SPEC-CHANNELS.md](SPEC-CHANNELS.md): Duplicate-work matching: scoring tiers,
  thresholds, and why a low score is never proof two agents will not collide.
- [SPEC-SUPERVISION.md](SPEC-SUPERVISION.md): Detecting a stalled subagent, with
  the measurements behind the thresholds.
- [PHILOSOPHY.md](PHILOSOPHY.md): Why Dibs reports and never acts. This is the
  boundary most design questions resolve against.
- [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md): The measured incident that defines the
  design.

## Using it

- [README.md](README.md): What it is, install, and the whole feature surface.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): The trust boundary is the machine. Read before
  pointing agents you do not trust at one daemon.
- [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md): Where to ask what.

## Optional

- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): What shipped when.
- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md): Argue with the work, not the person.
